panels.title: What the API serves (ClickHouse buckets)
panels.description: usage_buckets_15m with FINAL, i.e. after ReplacingMergeTree collapses row versions. This is the table Clickhouse::UsageBucket reads for current usage and wallet refresh.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count() AS "bucket rows", uniqExact(subscription_id) AS "subscriptions", uniqExact(organization_id) AS "orgs" FROM default.usage_buckets_15m FINAL

panels.title: Serving staleness (since last bucket write)
panels.description: now() - max(last_ingested_at). The wallet refresh waits (bounded) for this watermark to reach the trigger's ingested_at, so sustained growth here means the serving store is behind. Events whose payload omits ingested_at fall back to event_time (sql/05_usage.sql).

targets.rawSql: SELECT dateDiff('second', max(last_ingested_at), now()) AS staleness FROM default.usage_buckets_15m FINAL

panels.title: Correctness invariants (RisingWave) — both MUST be 0
panels.description: ROADMAP §0. over-count: more than one expanded row per (event identity, charge) — double billing. under-count: an enriched event that produced NO expanded row — silent event loss. Both are invisible in the served totals, which is why they are monitored here. A non-zero under-count can also be the known CDC-race gap (event with no subscription/charge yet).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(n - 1), 0) FROM (
     SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events_expanded
     GROUP BY organization_id, code, external_subscription_id, event_ts, transaction_id,
              COALESCE(charge_id, '')
     HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d) AS "over-count: extra rows",
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events_enriched e WHERE NOT EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM events_expanded x
     WHERE x.organization_id = e.organization_id AND x.code = e.code
       AND x.external_subscription_id = e.external_subscription_id
       AND x.event_ts = e.event_ts AND x.transaction_id = e.transaction_id))
     AS "under-count: dropped events";

panels.title: RisingWave working set (32-day window)
panels.description: The bounded firewall tables. Both are APPEND ONLY with retention_seconds = 33 days, so these counts plateau rather than grow forever; ClickHouse keeps the full history.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM events_enriched) AS "events_enriched", (SELECT count(*) FROM events_expanded) AS "events_expanded", (SELECT count(*) FROM usage_buckets_15m) AS "buckets (RW)";

panels.title: Usage per 15-minute bucket (ClickHouse)
panels.description: Event timestamp buckets, not write time — a late event updates an older bucket.

targets.rawSql: SELECT bucket AS time, concat(code, ' / ', if(charge_filter_id = '', 'default', charge_filter_id)) AS metric, toFloat64(sum(units)) AS units FROM default.usage_buckets_15m FINAL WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket) GROUP BY time, metric ORDER BY time

panels.title: Per-subscription serving state (ClickHouse buckets)
panels.description: Summed across the buckets in the dashboard time range — NOT a billing-period total; the API sums buckets over the period window Rails computes at read time.

targets.rawSql: SELECT subscription_id, code, aggregation_type, if(charge_filter_id = '', 'default', charge_filter_id) AS charge_filter, grouped_by, sum(events_count) AS events, toFloat64(sum(units)) AS units, max(last_event_at) AS last_event, max(last_ingested_at) AS last_write, dateDiff('second', max(last_ingested_at), now()) AS staleness_s FROM default.usage_buckets_15m FINAL WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket) GROUP BY subscription_id, code, aggregation_type, charge_filter, grouped_by ORDER BY last_write DESC LIMIT 50
